contributions.statement: When turning logged agent runs into a fixed workflow graph, or when checking dependencies an LLM planner proposed, add an edge only where a logged argument value of the consumer comes from an earlier call, and attribute it to the most recent eligible producer; never infer edges from call order, which was wrong for about 42% of adjacent pairs.
contributions.evidence: §6.5 Tables 2-3: on 15,775 def-use edges of T1's training split (synthetic travel dialogues, Wilson CIs), adjacency precision 0.584 (F1 0.711), frequency-thresholded directly-follows F1 0.712, argument co-reference + most-recent survivor 0.928/0.943; random survivor 0.403, earliest 0.146. Rows see different inputs and detection is trivial on this corpus.
relative_to: def-use data-flow analysis and data-aware process mining (Heuristics Miner limits)
2608.00267 agent plans recover only part of the source dependency DAG

contributions.statement: Before compiling a recurring agent task (for example a repeated ingestion runbook) into a deterministic workflow, measure the share of its calls that are schema/doc lookups or byte-identical repeats: that share bounds the saving and was about half of all calls per recurring scenario for one ReAct agent.
contributions.evidence: §6.2: census of 14,128 calls over 56 recurring AppWorld scenarios; per-scenario median removable 51.4% (IQR 41.9-74.1%), 51/56 above 30%; over-counts read-after-write and excludes compile cost, so it is an upper bound, not a realized saving.
relative_to: workflow memory / trajectory reduction (AWM, AgentDiet): agents re-derive known procedures

contributions.statement: When a compiled workflow step has an irreversible side effect whose branch or direction is not determined by the observed runs, leave it as an escalation point instead of compiling it.
contributions.evidence: §6.1/§6.3: one refusal (Spotify add vs remove) and one leave-one-out fold that escalated instead of paying the wrong recipient; no decline rate over the 56 scenarios.
relative_to: P19 human approval gates for irreversible actions

reason: Two moderate, measured refinements survive: derive workflow edges from argument data flow rather than call order (with a magnitude for how wrong order is), and size the payoff of compiling a recurring agent task by its lookup/repeat share. The end-to-end claim that compiled workflows beat the agent loop is not tested, so nothing here says a static graph outperforms the agent.
